summary.description: Triphenyltin compounds are colourless/white solids or liquids that are practically insoluble and primarily used as pesticides or biocides.
emission_sources: Use as fungicides in wood preservatives and crop protection
environmental_impact: Toxic to wildlife, especially aquatic organisms
Binds to soil and persists in the environment

top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Triphenyltin compounds are toxic to marine organisms and used in antifouling paints, making them particularly hazardous to aquatic ecosystems.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: The persistence and bioaccumulation of triphenyltin compounds in the environment highlight the need for sustainable chemical management and production practices.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Triphenyltin compounds can contaminate aquatic environments and persist in sediments, threatening clean water access and ecosystem health.
